title: Quick check: Understanding React Rendering Architectures

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Understanding React Rendering Architectures”?
options: The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Client-side rendering depends on the selected React framework/runtime and must respect server/client boundaries.
The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
questions.answer_key: Client-side rendering depends on the selected React framework/runtime and must respect server/client boundaries.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Understanding React Rendering Architectures: Client-side rendering depends on the selected React framework/runtime and must respect server/client boundaries.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Client-side rendering?
options: Confirm the chosen framework supports the API and keep server-only dependencies out of client bundles.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
questions.answer_key: Confirm the chosen framework supports the API and keep server-only dependencies out of client bundles.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Understanding React Rendering Architectures: Confirm the chosen framework supports the API and keep server-only dependencies out of client bundles.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Understanding React Rendering Architectures” complete?
options: Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Understanding React Rendering Architectures: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
